subject: Biology
title: Whale Songs
description: A fast breakdown of Whale Songs for builders.

hook.text: Humpback whales sing complex songs lasting up to 20 minutes and repeat them for hours.

buildup.text: Only males sing, suggesting the songs play a role in mating or territorial display.

discovery.text: All males in a population sing the same song, and it gradually changes over the season.

twist.text: New song elements spread between populations across oceans—a form of cultural transmission.

climax.text: Low-frequency whale calls can travel thousands of kilometers through deep ocean channels.

punchline.text: A concert heard across an entire ocean.

quiz.question: How long can a humpback whale song last?

details.summary: Humpback whale songs are complex, structured vocal performances lasting up to 30 minutes that are repeated for hours. All males in a population sing the same song, which gradually changes through the season, with new versions spreading across oceans.
details.whyItMatters: Whale songs demonstrate cultural evolution in a non-human species. Songs change progressively, spread between populations, and follow trends, revealing that whales participate in shared, evolving acoustic traditions.
takeaways: All males in a humpback population share the same song at any time
Songs evolve progressively throughout the breeding season
New song elements spread between ocean populations over years

faq.question: Why do humpback whales sing?
faq.answer: Only males sing, primarily during breeding season, suggesting a role in mate attraction or male competition. Songs may advertise fitness, establish territory, or coordinate spacing between males. The exact function is still debated among researchers.

faq.question: How do whale songs spread between populations?
faq.answer: Songs from one population can spread to neighboring populations over several years, moving eastward across the Pacific. Males that hear new song elements from visitors or during migration incorporate them, creating cultural waves of musical change.
